title: The Oracle against Moab: Balak and Balaam
english: Having fully finished his discourse on the Babylonians and the Philistines, he now turns his prophecy to Moab, that is, against the capital city of the Moabites, the whole country, and the kingdom itself. They too were a barbarous nation, hateful to God, because they were wholly given over to the worship of idols, trusted above all in the art of magic, exalted themselves against the glory of God, and were among the bitterest enemies of the people of Israel.

Indeed, when the Israelites had been freed from the greed of the Egyptians and were going to the land of promise, they very nearly all perished, as far as the scheme of Balak, then king of the Moabites, could bring it about. It is written thus in Numbers: “And all the sons of Israel encamped on the west of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho. And Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorite; and Moab was greatly afraid of the people, because they were many; and Moab was filled with dread before the sons of Israel” (Numbers 22:1-3).

Then what was his wicked scheme? He hired Balaam from Mesopotamia, a false prophet and an augur, and then appealed to him, saying: “Curse Israel for me. For I know,” he says, “that those whom you bless are blessed, and those whom you curse are cursed” (Numbers 22:6). So Balaam went through his ways of sorcery, with altars set up and sacrifices offered (Numbers 23:1-2). But Balak was cheated of his hope and missed his aim, for the man brought in to curse them unexpectedly blessed Israel (Numbers 24:10).

When his attempt had turned out contrary to his hopes, he pursued his malice against them again by another way. For he caught the Israelites as in a net, carried away by the beauty of the women, so that they forsook their love for God and chose to worship Baal of Peor, an idol of the Moabites. It is written thus again in Numbers: “And Israel lodged at Shittim, and the people were defiled by committing fornication with the daughters of Moab; and they invited them to the sacrifices of their idols, and the people ate of their sacrifices and bowed down to their idols. And Israel was initiated into the rites of Baal of Peor, and the Lord was angry with Israel in His wrath” (Numbers 25:1-3).
